evals.name: synthesize-from-durable-state
evals.prompt: Where were we? Catch me up on this session.
evals.expected_output: The skill produces a read-only briefing that goes beyond the conversation: it resolves and reads the durable memory-tier state (handoff save-points, workflow checklist, running-retro ledgers) plus git and any open PRs/work-items, then synthesizes a goal/why, where-we-stand, decisions-made, and direction briefing. It writes nothing.
expectations: Reads durable state (handoffs / workflow checklist / running-retro / git / PRs), not just the conversation
Synthesizes a briefing covering goal-why, where-we-stand, decisions-made, and direction
Grounds claims in reads made this turn rather than remembered state
Writes nothing and does not /clear or end the session

evals.name: adds-durable-layer-beyond-recap
evals.prompt: Give me the state of play — and I already ran /recap, so don't just repeat the conversation.
evals.expected_output: The skill explains it complements /recap by adding the durable + off-thread layer /recap cannot see (on-disk ledgers/handoffs, open PRs, off-thread work), rather than re-summarizing only the conversation. It does not attempt to invoke the built-in /recap (built-ins are not Skill-invocable).
expectations: Adds durable + off-thread state beyond a conversation-only summary
Does not attempt to call the built-in /recap from the skill
Delivers a distinct value (on-disk state, PRs, in-flight work), not a recap echo

evals.name: read-only-routes-not-acts
evals.prompt: Where do we stand? And there were some background jobs running — pick them back up while you're at it.
evals.expected_output: The skill gives the read-only orientation and reports the off-thread work at a glance, but does NOT recover or resume it — it routes recovery to /session-flow:keep-going. It also does not prescribe the next stage (that is /session-flow:workflow) or write anything.
expectations: Delivers the read-only briefing and names the off-thread work
Does NOT itself inspect, resume, or restart the background jobs
Routes recovery to /session-flow:keep-going rather than acting
Writes nothing

evals.name: freshness-doubt-routes-to-reanchor
evals.prompt: Brief me on where we are — but this session is resuming a plan from three days ago, some of it may be out of date.
evals.expected_output: The skill synthesizes the current-state briefing from the durable state, reports those claims AS claims (e.g. 'the handoff says X'), and because freshness is in doubt it points to /session-flow:reanchor to verify the assumptions still hold rather than asserting the stale state as current fact. It does not run the drift verification itself.
expectations: Reports durable-state claims as claims, not as verified current fact
Points to /session-flow:reanchor to verify freshness when it is in doubt
Does not itself perform the freshness/drift verification
Still delivers the orientation briefing

evals.name: catch-up-opens-with-needs-you
evals.prompt: /session-flow:orient catch-up. (Since my last message two subagents returned results and two decisions are waiting on me: which API shape to ship, and whether to approve the force-push to the release branch. The chat also touched one open pull request.)
evals.expected_output: The skill runs the catch-up scope, anchored at the user's last own message. The reply opens with a Needs you section that gives the count 2, then says what happened with what each result means, then covers each of the two action items with the decision, why it matters now, the options and their costs, a recommendation, and what happens if the user does not answer. It re-checks pull requests and CI the chat touched read-only, keeps What happened within the word cap, and writes nothing.
expectations: Opens with a Needs you section that states 2 action items
Gives each action item a recommendation and an if-unanswered line
Lists what happened most important first, each result with what it means for the user
Re-checks the state of touched pull requests and CI read-only, saying what could not be checked
Keeps What happened within the word cap and writes nothing

evals.name: catch-up-nothing-happened
evals.prompt: /session-flow:orient catch-up. (Nothing has run since my last message, and nothing is waiting on me.)
evals.expected_output: The skill runs the catch-up scope, finds nothing happened since the user's last message and no action item waiting, says so in the Needs you section, and stops without padding the reply with a four-part briefing.
expectations: Says in the Needs you section that there are no action items
Says nothing happened since the user's last message
Stops there, without a four-part briefing or invented content
Writes nothing

evals.name: zoom-out-timeline-from-handoff-chain
evals.prompt: Zoom out for me: when did we start on the invoice export, and what did we do each day? (The working tree is on branch feat/invoice-export. The handoffs directory holds the four handoff files in this case's fixtures, one chain on topic invoice-export. No spec container is linked and no plan file is named.)
evals.expected_output: The skill runs the zoom-out scope. Its first line names the boundary it used: the branch feat/invoice-export, since no spec container resolves. It reads the newest handoff (2026-09-04) and its four-entry chain, and lists all four sessions with date, session id, did and left matching the handoffs: 2026-09-01 (1b6f2c3e, endpoint scaffolded / rounding and pagination left), 2026-09-02 twice (4c8d9e10 rounding fixed; 7e0a1b22 pagination landed and PR #41 opened), and 2026-09-04 (9f1b2c33, review fixes pushed / docs page and release note left). It says the effort started 2026-09-01, groups sessions by day, and checks git, merged PRs and /session-flow:recall for 2026-09-03, which has no handoff, showing that day only if a source has something for it. Near term lists the docs page and release note from the newest handoff's remaining actions. Every claim carries a source label, and the reply ends with the newest handoff's one open question (whether the export includes voided invoices) restated with both options, their costs and the recommendation to include them with a status column. A timeline visual is only offered and routed to /visualization:visualize, and nothing is written.
expectations: Names the effort boundary it used (the branch feat/invoice-export) and says the effort started on 2026-09-01
Lists all four sessions, each with its date, session id, did and left matching the handoff files, grouped by day with both 2026-09-02 sessions under that day
Checks git and merged pull requests for 2026-09-03, the day with no handoff, and runs /session-flow:recall for it, without opening a transcript file
Labels every claim with its source (handoff file, git, tracker, plan, recall or conversation)
Near term matches the newest handoff's remaining actions (docs page, release note)
Ends with the recorded open question on voided invoices, restated with both options, their costs and a recommendation, and invents no other decision
Writes nothing, and only offers a timeline visual through /visualization:visualize rather than writing one to disk

evals.name: zoom-out-container-plan-and-disagreement
evals.prompt: /session-flow:orient zoom-out. (The working tree is on branch feat/ledger-sync. Its work item #212 links the open spec container #200, created 2026-10-03, which /work-items:track can read. The conversation names the plan file in this case's fixtures. The handoffs directory holds the two handoff files in the fixtures, one chain on topic ledger-sync.)
evals.expected_output: The skill runs the zoom-out scope. Its first line names the boundary it used: the spec container #200, which wins over the branch feat/ledger-sync and the plan file because it comes first in the boundary order. It says the effort started 2026-10-03, the container's creation, and gives the chain root's 2026-10-05 as the other candidate. It lists both sessions (2026-10-05 2a7c4e51 and 2026-10-07 5d8e9f02) and reports that the 2026-10-07 handoff's Prior sessions row for 2026-10-05 (conflict resolution done, backfill left) disagrees with the 2026-10-05 file it names (retry policy agreed, webhook receiver and conflict resolution left), giving both with their labels and pointing to /session-flow:reanchor. It runs /session-flow:recall for the days with no handoff. Near term lists the plan's open Phase 2 (conflict resolution, with its precondition) beside the newest handoff's remaining action (wire the receiver to the sync worker); long term lists Phase 3 (backfill). It says no open decision is recorded, and writes nothing.
expectations: Names the spec container #200 as the effort boundary, not the branch or the plan file
Says the effort started on 2026-10-03, the container's creation, and gives the chain root's 2026-10-05 as the other candidate
Reports that the 2026-10-07 handoff's Prior sessions row for 2026-10-05 disagrees with the 2026-10-05 handoff file, gives both versions with their source labels, and points to /session-flow:reanchor
Near term includes the plan's open Phase 2 (conflict resolution) as well as the newest handoff's remaining action (wire the webhook receiver to the sync worker)
Long term includes the plan's later Phase 3 (backfill)
Runs /session-flow:recall for the days with no handoff, without opening a transcript file
Says no open decision is recorded and invents none, and writes nothing
